question: If cos θ = (12)/(13), then the value of (sin theta(1-tan theta))/(tan theta(1+cosec theta)) is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify triplet (5, 12, 13) since cos θ = 12/13 (Base/Hypotenuse), so Perpendicular = 5.

Simplify Expression: [sin θ (1 − tan θ)] / [tan θ (1 + cosec θ)] = [cos θ (1 − tan θ)] / (1 + cosec θ).

Substitute values: [(12/13) × (1 − 5/12)] / (1 + 13/5).

Calculation: [(12/13) × (7/12)] ÷ (18/5) = (7/13) × (5/18) = 35/234.

**∴ The correct answer is 35/234.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: cos θ = 12/13

Formula: cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse | sin θ = Perp / Hyp | tan θ = Perp / Base | cosec θ = Hyp / Perp

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5363c33c5bfa11aee7dcb4da636b610113ceeb0777f31047f4af1b9d9873271a.png] 

⇒ Base (B) = 12, Hypotenuse (H) = 13, Perpendicular (P) = 5

⇒ sin θ = 5/13

⇒ tan θ = 5/12

⇒ cosec θ = 13/5

⇒ Numerator = sin θ(1 − tan θ) = (5/13) × (1 − 5/12) = (5/13) × (7/12) = 35/156

⇒ Denominator = tan θ(1 + cosec θ) = (5/12) × (1 + 13/5) = (5/12) × (18/5) = 18/12 = 3/2

⇒ Result = (35/156) ÷ (3/2) = (35/156) × (2/3) = 35 / (78 × 3) = 35/234

**∴ The correct answer is 35/234.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

Standard ratios: sin θ = P/H, cos θ = B/H, tan θ = P/B, cot θ = B/P, sec θ = H/B, cosec θ = H/P.

Reciprocal Identities

sin θ = 1/cosec θ, cos θ = 1/sec θ, tan θ = 1/cot θ = sin θ / cos θ.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common sets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25) satisfy P² + B² = H².</p
